- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile (e.g., post-0.29 sentiment bump).
- Underestimate downward moves when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.70 or -0.67) — model tends to lag or underreact.
- When sentiment is mildly negative (-0.10 to -0.30), model often overcorrects upward, leading to overshoots in early forecast days.
- Mean reversion bias: model frequently overpredicts mid-term highs and underpredicts lows — adjust for 3-5 day smoothing in trend.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slope or add dampening factor.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid assuming linear continuation — model often fails to capture sudden sentiment-driven reversals (e.g., -0.40 → +0.07 → sharp drop).
